summary: Uses Digital and IT’s mature-team estimate as the high-water mobilisation ceiling, incorporating the confirmed 50/50 Product Manager allocation and James Costerton’s Year One architecture phasing while keeping D365 and remaining specialist/service questions explicit.
detailSummary:
The Digital and IT high-water model remains the prudent mobilisation ceiling, but confirmed reductions are applied as evidence becomes available. Jon Ward has confirmed the permanent 1.0 FTE Product Manager should be funded 50/50 between Student and Staff Hubs. James Costerton has now clarified that Solution Architect / Technical Lead input was intended to average 0.75 FTE across Year One, front-loaded from full-time input and tapering through 0.5 and 0.25 as the architecture settles. At the current G7 rate this reduces the Year One architecture provision from £54,016 to £40,512. Years Two and Three remain at the previous full-year high-water provision until the enduring architecture model is agreed.

James has also clarified that the Dynamics / D365 Developer line was a prudent finger-in-the-air allowance rather than a defined Student Hub requirement. Some D365 / Power Platform work may be needed if specific King’s Edge or Hub MVP capabilities require it, but some or all may be deliverable through the core R&C CRM team. The cash provision therefore remains in the high-water envelope, but it is explicitly an MVP-dependent contingency rather than a settled dedicated Hub role.

Jon Ward’s six-month recruitment and steady-onboarding assumption remains a mobilisation constraint. Recruitment lag is not booked automatically as a saving because the gap may require contractors or reprioritised existing Digital and IT capacity. Infuse remains confirmed outsourced non-pay QA/testing at £6,000 per month.

James considers the current Azure/platform and student-facing AI runtime envelopes reasonable high-water assumptions. They remain planning envelopes rather than forecasts and should be refined from architecture, usage and unit-cost evidence. The £90,000 Devin/Cognition allowance remains fully attributed to the Student Hub for now: James expects one 4,000-ACU instance to provide useful AI-first development capacity but cannot yet support a defensible pro-rata split.

After applying the Year One Solution Architect phasing, the Student Hub high-water profile is £593,360 in 2026/27, £876,296 in 2027/28 and £926,296 in 2028/29: £2,395,952 across mobilisation, leaving £604,048 headroom within the £3.0m strategic envelope. The recurrent Student Hub risk ceiling remains £893,296 per year before the enduring 4.1.1 knowledge/content operating model because the architecture clarification is a Year One phasing decision, not yet a settled BAU reduction.
